 Is it useful to measure “biological” age?


 Sam Wikeley

Science correspondent


 I used to work in theoretical physics, where it was not uncommon to spend lunch chatting with colleagues about time forming a loop or perhaps having an extra dimension. While those ideas are not as outlandish as they may sound, in the harsh reality of everyday life, time appears to pass in only one direction: forward. This means that as far as my chronological age is concerned, I’m not getting any younger.
